topic: Least-favourable face-multiplier inference for sharp survivor-complier benefit bounds. Fix finite covariate support J>=2 and ordered outcome support K>=3 in the conditional-IV model with consistency, exclusion, no defiers, weak cellwise selection monotonicity, fixed covariate and instrument-overlap lower bounds, aggregate survivor-complier mass bounded away from zero, and a nonredundant raw-capacity covariance eigenvalue band; impose no lower bound on individual cell survivor masses, no sign margin on the survivor-mass gap, and no Ferrers-cut separation. Starting from the banked exact selected-complier partial-transport capacities and closed sharp benefit endpoints, use the unscreened nonnegative-projection plug-in and define the least-favourable survivor-support face envelope by retaining every capacity, zero-gap, survivor-minimum, lower-cut, upper-cut, and mass-cap branch within a_n, where a_n tends to zero and sqrt(n)a_n tends to infinity. Prove that the conditional multiplier quantile of the finite retained-gradient maximum gives uniform root-n coverage of the entire sharp identified interval over triangular arrays with simultaneous ties and changing survivor support, without deterministic padding; prove oracle face-envelope equivalence on separated faces; and prove strict asymptotic undercoverage of calibration that keeps only the empirical maximizing/minimizing branches and empirically positive survivor cells on the specified two-covariate, three-outcome contiguous witness. Computation must use the explicit finite min-cut branch gradients and no latent LP. Consumer: the Chen-Flores Job Corps principal-stratification wage analysis, which could report honest uncertainty for the fraction of always-employed compliers whose ordered wage improves. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: an unconditional-capacity reparameterization makes both endpoints finite piecewise linear-fractional maps; a finite pathwise secant-gradient argument dominates both signed endpoint errors by retained gradients. The legal changing-support witness keeps raw-capacity contrast covariance eigenvalues in [1/4,1], and direct Gaussian-limit diagnostics show material single-face undercoverage; checks covered the active upper mass cap, denominator derivatives, projection-release directions, screening bias, zero-gradient calibration, and generic directional-inference collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: certify that the explicit Gaussian witness has rejection probability above 0.4 at nominal alpha=0.4; the derived finite branch decomposition reduces this to Gaussian polyhedral probabilities. EARLY KILL TEST: independently implement and certify a lower bound exceeding 0.4 for the conservative Gaussian rejection event at kappa=1; failure after correcting the implementation should pivot the witness claim or stop the kernel. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/presolve_pid_slate_benefit_face_multiplier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a least-favourable multiplier envelope over every empirically near-active capacity, zero-gap, survivor-minimum, cut, and mass-cap face deliver uniform root-n coverage of both sharp survivor-complier ordinal-benefit endpoints when faces tie and cellwise survivor support changes?

source_refs.claim: Sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds are available, but ordinary bootstrap inference undercovers near boundary faces and the proposed m-out-of-n repair is conservative.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: The paper bounds mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers and notes that its simple interval applies where bounding functions lack min/max operators.
source_refs.author: Xuan Chen and Carlos A. Flores

source_refs.claim: Root-n debiased inference is developed for intensive-margin complier-effect bounds under weak sample-selection monotonicity, but not for survivor-complier ordinal benefit.
source_refs.author: Yingying Dong and Phillip Heiler

source_refs.excerpt: supplies neither uniform anti-concentration nor an observable common-multiplier coupling through variance degeneracy.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The benefit-bound literature documents boundary undercoverage but uses conservative subsampling, while the closest Job Corps principal-stratification work concerns mean effects or smoother bounding functions. The prior-proposal record independently identifies the missing uniform anti-concentration and observable common-multiplier coupling through degeneracy. Here each endpoint is a ratio of nested finite min/max and nonnegative-projection branches. With n^{-1/2}-local ties or survivor masses approaching zero, its derivative is a maximum over a drifting face set; a single empirical optimizer and a fixed-support delta method omit relevant signed directions. The presolve claims that an unconditional-capacity parameterization and finite secant-gradient domination solve this problem remain hypotheses requiring independent proof.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array theorem proving that the conditional quantile of the maximum of all signed gradients retained within a_n, where a_n tends to zero and sqrt(n)a_n tends to infinity, gives uniform asymptotic coverage of the entire sharp interval without deterministic padding.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation connects imperfect compliance and employment selection directly to policy-relevant inference for always-employed Job Corps compliers.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Job Corps affects enrollment and employment -> wages are observed only for workers under imperfect compliance -> always-employed compliers are the policy-facing stratum -> honest uncertainty is needed for their probability of wage improvement

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt inequality selection and Gaussian critical values for extrema, including the proof that near-binding inequalities dominate endpoint error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The survivor-benefit endpoints are finite intersection bounds whose candidate inequalities are explicit capacity and cut faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and resample the directional derivative of a nonsmooth map, using local analysis of all active directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite min/max compositions of linear-fractional faces are directionally differentiable at ties but generally not fully differentiable.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian and conditional multiplier approximation for maxima of correlated sample-mean coordinates, supported by anti-concentration bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After face retention, simultaneous signed endpoint error is bounded by a finite maximum of correlated raw-capacity gradients.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one certify, on an explicit two-covariate three-outcome contiguous Gaussian experiment with legal raw-capacity covariance, that calibration using only empirical optimizing faces and empirically positive survivor cells has rejection probability strictly above 0.4 at nominal alpha 0.4?

source_refs.claim: With a Gaussian first-stage limit, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary-bootstrap consistency, so max-type derivatives at ties can invalidate calibration.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Direct bootstrap construction of confidence-interval endpoints defined by moment inequalities is invalid in general, including uniformly asymptotically.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Sukjin Han

source_refs.claim: Simulations for symbolic probability-of-benefit bounds show ordinary-bootstrap undercoverage when a true endpoint lies on or near a boundary.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.excerpt: quantify the two observable-outcome support probabilities, conditional variance, branch/failure-region mass

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing negative results establish generic inconsistency or simulation undercoverage, but not a fully legal survivor-complier distribution with changing support, bounded overlap, positive aggregate target mass, and nonredundant raw-capacity covariance eigenvalues in the required band. The prior reviewer record also demands an explicit nondegeneracy audit based on support probabilities, conditional variance, and failure-region mass. For the proposed witness, strict undercoverage depends on a correlated Gaussian probability over a finite union of polyhedra after accounting for denominator derivatives, projection-release directions, zero-gradient calibration, and both endpoint signs. Numerical diagnostics alone do not certify the required probability inequality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit triangular array and covariance matrix, together with an analytic or interval-arithmetic certificate proving that the limiting Gaussian-polyhedral rejection probability at kappa 1 is strictly greater than 0.4.

writing_exemplar.why: It turns a nonregularity concern into a transparent counterexample and sharply distinguishes invalid direct endpoint resampling from valid alternatives.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Endpoint estimators choose binding inequalities -> empirical selection changes discontinuously under local drift -> direct resampling misses relevant local configurations -> a legal survivor-benefit witness proves strict undercoverage

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce bootstrap failure to nonlinearity of the directional derivative under a Gaussian first-stage limit and compare the plug-in law with the correct local law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The empirical optimizer uses one linear face whereas the true tie derivative maximizes over several faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct contiguous moment-inequality examples and calculate their nonuniform endpoint-coverage failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate is an equally explicit endpoint-undercoverage counterexample specialized to a sharp survivor-complier benefit interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent maximum events through Gaussian rectangle or polyhedral probabilities and control their approximation using anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the two-by-three witness is fixed, branch selection and rejection are finite systems of affine Gaussian inequalities.

open_problems.open_problem: Under quantitative separation of all inactive endpoint branches and all zero survivor-mass faces, is the near-face multiplier envelope asymptotically identical to an oracle calibration that knows the population active face and survivor support?

source_refs.claim: Refined moment selection discards sufficiently slack inequalities while preserving asymptotic validity and improving critical values.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Panle Jia Barwick

source_refs.claim: Inference for optimized value functions uses estimated directional derivatives because marginal optimization is not fully Hadamard differentiable.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Antonio F. Galvao, and Thomas Parker

source_refs.claim: Generalized moment selection obtains uniform size while adapting critical values to inequalities inferred to be slack.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Gustavo Soares

open_problems.why_unsolved: Moment-selection results screen normalized slack inequalities, while optimized-value results estimate argmax-based directional derivatives. The survivor-complier map adds interacting discontinuities from nonnegative projection and the appearance or disappearance of cell-specific ratio branches as survivor mass reaches zero. The missing selection lemma must show simultaneously that every population-active cut and support face is retained and every quantitatively separated face is deleted despite estimated denominators and nested extrema.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem showing equality with probability tending to one between the retained empirical gradient set and the oracle population face set, and consequently an o_p(1) difference between their conditional multiplier quantiles.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames inference through an optimization map's argmax geometry and separates general validity from sharper behavior under regular configurations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Econometric bounds are optimized value functions -> multiple optimizers create nondifferentiability -> directional-derivative resampling restores validity -> separated survivor-support faces should permit oracle-equivalent calibration

method_exemplars.technique: Use a diverging but sub-root-n selection threshold and uniform probability bounds for retaining binding moments while deleting separated slack moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The a_n face envelope uses the same intermediate-rate selection logic, with explicit endpoint branches replacing moment inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt refined selection arguments quantifying the power and uniformity consequences of removing slack constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Oracle equivalence asserts precisely that separated irrelevant branches can be removed without changing first-order calibration.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt numerical directional differentiation with an intermediate step size and its uniform-validity proof for convex Lipschitz maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its intermediate-rate derivative approximation is structurally analogous to retaining every endpoint face in an a_n neighborhood.

open_problems.open_problem: Can finite face-envelope inference for survivor-complier ordinal-benefit bounds be extended to high-dimensional or continuous covariates by orthogonalizing every raw capacity and applying near-active-face retention after cross-fitting?

source_refs.claim: Efficient orthogonal moments and debiased machine learning provide root-n inference for intensive-margin complier-effect bounds under weak sample-selection monotonicity and flexible covariates.
source_refs.author: Yingying Dong and Phillip Heiler

source_refs.claim: Generalized Lee bounds permit covariate-varying selection direction and provide uniform Gaussian support-function inference with flexible nuisance estimation.
source_refs.author: Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: Closed symbolic probability-of-benefit bounds are developed for ordinal outcomes, without combining survivor principal strata and orthogonal machine-learning nuisance estimation.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The scan found orthogonal inference for selected-complier mean bounds and symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds in separate literatures, but no theorem combining them. The donor DML argument begins with smooth scalar bound scores; the first changed step is construction of a jointly orthogonal score vector for every ordered-outcome cut capacity and survivor-mass denominator. A resolution must then couple the cross-fitted first stage to a nonsmooth projection and a drifting near-face set, including covariate regions whose survivor mass approaches zero.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cross-fitted estimator with orthogonal scores for all raw capacities and a theorem giving uniform root-n conditional-multiplier coverage of the sharp survivor-complier benefit interval under explicit nuisance-rate and face-retention conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination-area narrative and the policy relevance of the Job Corps always-employed-complier population.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Job Corps enrollment is endogenous to assignment -> wages are selected by employment -> always-employed compliers are the relevant principal stratum -> flexible covariate adjustment should support inference on their probability of wage improvement

method_exemplars.technique: Derive efficient orthogonal moments for selected-complier bound components, cross-fit nuisance estimates, and prove root-n debiased inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It has the same endogenous-treatment and weak-selection-monotonicity structure; the new target replaces mean-bound components with ordinal transport capacities.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate covariate-indexed selection signs and bound components with regularized nuisances, then conduct uniform Gaussian inference on the identified-set support function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies flexible-covariate machinery that must be combined with the survivor-benefit map's face-wise gradients.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap an estimated directional derivative rather than the original nonsmooth plug-in map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Orthogonal first-stage scores do not remove the finite min/max nondifferentiability of the final sharp endpoint.

literature_map:
Chen and Flores (2015, JBES) combine noncompliance and employment selection for Job Corps, but target mean wages for always-employed compliers.
Dong and Heiler (2026, arXiv:2606.09223) sharpen intensive-margin complier bounds under weak selection monotonicity and add efficient orthogonal root-n inference.
Zhang and Rubin (2003) and Imai (2008) are foundational truncation-by-death and survivor-average-effect bound papers; Imai uses a contaminated-data representation for sharpness.
Long and Hudgens (2013, Biometrics) show categorical baseline covariates can strictly sharpen principal-effect bounds and characterize when they do.
Lee (2009, ReStud) gives trimming bounds and wage inference under selection; Semenova (2025, JoE) permits covariate-varying selection direction and uniform support-function inference.
Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS) derive sharp probabilities-of-benefit and no-harm bounds for ordinal outcomes, including complier extensions under monotonicity.
Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024, Biometrika) give symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds under imperfect randomization, but ordinary-bootstrap intervals undercover near boundary faces.
Fan and Park (2010), Russell (2021), Frandsen (2021), and Ober-Reynolds (arXiv:2311.09435) connect treatment-effect-distribution functionals to sharp coupling or optimal-transport bounds and inference.
Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013, Econometrica) develop adaptive intersection-bound inference and document extrema-selection bias.
Andrews and Soares (2010) and Andrews and Barwick (2012) develop generalized and refined moment selection; Andrews, Roth, and Pakes (2023, ReStud) combine least-favourable and conditional calibration.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud) characterize ordinary-bootstrap failure for directionally differentiable maps; Hong and Li (2018, JoE) provide numerical directional differentiation.
Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, JoE) estimate directional derivatives for optimized value functions and obtain uniform inference.
Andrews and Han (2009, Econometrics Journal) prove direct endpoint-bootstrap failure in moment-inequality models, but the literature lacks a certified legal two-covariate, three-outcome survivor-benefit witness and a no-padding face-envelope theorem under simultaneous ties and changing support.
